ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory onboarding and ongoing screening of all partners, general partner principals, authorized signatories and 25%+ UBOs against: (a) the UN Consolidated Security Council List under the United Nations Act; (b) Global Affairs Canada sanctioned persons and entities under the Special Economic Measures Act; (c) FINTRAC risk assessments and RCMP Criminal Code Part II.1 designations; (d) the U.S. OFAC SDN list as best-practice cross-border benchmark; (e) EU consolidated sanctions where the target market includes EU clients. Domestic and foreign PEPs are identified per FINTRAC definitions, triggering enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification and senior management approval. Suspicious transaction reports are filed with FINTRAC within 30 days; terrorist property reports are filed within 24 hours. Client and UBO records must be retained for a minimum of five years after the last transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry / RegistryXpress online portal operated by Service Alberta and authorized registry agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in Latin script (English or French). Alberta accepts 'and', '&', 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.' or 'LP' as statutory designators. No non-Latin transliteration is recognized for provincial registration; extra-provincial names must be translated or transliterated into an acceptable Latin-alphabet form. The name must be distinguishable from all existing corporations, limited partnerships, trade names and registered extra-provincial entities in Alberta per the Partnership Act and Business Names Registration Act.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Immigration (requires CICC-authorized RCIC or law society member before use)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its authorized registry agent must submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar (Service Alberta, Corporate Registry) through RegistryXpress within 30 days of the rejection notice, stating grounds of distinctiveness and attaching supporting consent letters or ministerial approvals. If administrative reconsideration fails, the applicant may file a re-application with a new NUANS-style search or seek judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Business Corporations Act and common law principles of procedural fairness. Sensitive tokens such as 'College', 'University' or 'Immigration' require a prior written ministerial or CICC authorization letter which must be attached at the time of re-filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the statutory registered office address in Alberta provided a physical Albertan street address is maintained and mail forwarding is reliable. However, for an international student placement and immigration visa consultancy, CICC professional conduct standards and FINTRAC AML record-keeping expectations require an actual operational presence, client interview space and secure records storage under the supervision of a licensed RCIC; a hybrid model (physical RCIC office plus virtual administrative address) is acceptable, but a purely nominal virtual office without an operating professional on site is not compliant for this regulated industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Enhanced risk quantification: approximately 35% cumulative probability of a CICC practice inspection or FINTRAC compliance examination within the first 36 months of operation; unannounced physical on-site check probability is approximately 10-15% for this Medium_Risk_Enhanced immigration consultancy sector, and materially higher if UBO transparency gaps, cash-equivalent payments or escrow irregularities are detected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3 (Alberta), Part 2 — Limited Partnerships, ss. 51-73, including the formation, contribution, filing, and registration requirements for limited partnerships; supplemental requirements under the Partnership Amendment Rules and Alberta Business Corporations Act for any corporate general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta — Registrar of Corporations and Business Names (Sir Frederick W. Haultain Building, Edmonton, Alberta; corporate registry e-filing service).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration for Registration of a Limited Partnership (filed under s. 53 of the Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3), resulting in issuance of the Certificate of Limited Partnership and assignment of the limited partnership registration number.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an Alberta limited partnership. The Declaration must state the aggregate actual capital contribution of the limited partners, which may be contributed in cash, property, or services as set out in the partnership agreement. No escrow or mandatory capital-holding account is required at formation; however, for immigration-client work under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) rules, all client funds must be held in a segregated Canadian trust/escrow account maintained by a regulated financial institution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST, that the General Partner approves the formation and registration of [●] Limited Partnership under the Partnership Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 2; RESOLVED SECOND, that the partnership’s registered office is fixed at [Address], Calgary, Alberta, T2P 1M4, being a suitable address for service of process; RESOLVED THIRD, that the General Partner is authorized to execute the Declaration for Registration and all ancillary filings with the Alberta Corporate Registry; RESOLVED FOURTH, that [Name] is appointed as Initial Compliance and Trust Account Officer, solely empowered to open a segregated client trust account compliant with CICC trust rules; RESOLVED FIFTH, that all registration fees, notarial costs, and post-formation compliance expenditures be ratified and paid from the partnership’s contributed capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Service Alberta (Corporate Registry Name Reservation window and NUANS name search service).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS availability search with the Alberta Corporate Registry; propose up to three distinctive trade names for the limited partnership; submit a Name Reservation Request through the Corporate Registry portal; upon approval, record the 90-day reservation (renewable once) before filing the Declaration. Ensure the name contains neither 'Limited' as a full word nor any prohibited element for a limited partnership and that the reservation certificate is appended to the later registration filing.
required_dossiers: NUANS Preliminary Name Search Report
Name Reservation Request form completed online
Letter of authorization from the intended General Partner
Identity and address evidence of the subscribing partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of confusion, misdescription, or contravention of Regulation 73(1), promptly file a revised Name Reservation Request with alternative names; a written reconsideration may be submitted within 10 business days, and an amendment to the reservation can be processed without forfeiting the priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare the Limited Partnership Declaration and Partnership Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Service Alberta; external legal counsel and notary public for execution witnessing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Declaration for Registration of a Limited Partnership under Part 2 of the Partnership Act, setting out the proposed name, Alberta registered office address, nature of business (International Student Placement and Golden Visa Residence Advisory), full names and addresses of the general partners and limited partners, and the aggregate limited-partner capital contributions. Execute the Declaration by the General Partner and have the execution witnessed or notarized; concurrently adopt the pro-forma first board resolution of the General Partner and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement covering profit-sharing, capital calls, and CICC compliance obligations.
required_dossiers: Draft Declaration for Registration of a Limited Partnership
Pro-forma first board resolution of the corporate General Partner
Notarized copy of the General Partner's incorporating certificate (where a corporate general partner is used)
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Consent of the registered office provider and address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries incomplete partner details, contribution particulars, or office-address validity, file an amended Declaration with supplemental affidavits within 30 days of the notice; if the query relates to the general partner's standing, submit the general partner's certificate of good standing to cure the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Declaration and Pay the Statutory Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Service Alberta (online Companies E-Filing portal or counter service at the Edmonton Registry office / authorized registry agent).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Declaration by e-filing or in person with a cover letter referencing the Name Reservation Certificate; pay the prescribed filing fee of CAD 100 (approximately USD 73) by credit card, debt card, or certified cheque; upon acceptance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Limited Partnership and a unique registration number. Retain the certified copy and ensure the public record shows a valid Alberta registered office and the active general partner designation.
required_dossiers: Executed Declaration for Registration of a Limited Partnership
Alberta Corporate Registry filing fee receipt
Name Reservation Certificate (if previously obtained)
Notarized witness or execution affidavit(s)
Cover letter identifying authorized filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused or queried, the Registry issues a notice of defect specifying the deficiency; cure by filing an amended Declaration and required proof, usually without losing the original priority; for urgent transactional deadlines, a same-day expedited re-filing service is available for an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for the CRA Business Number, GST/HST, and Payroll Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and Business Window telephone service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the LP registration number, file a Business Registration Online application with the CRA; obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and Program Account codes for GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), and any other applicable accounts; elect the partnership's fiscal year-end and confirm that the Canadian-resident general partner or tax representative will file the annual partnership Information Return (Form T5013). Maintain a written CRA account authorization designating the managing partner.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Limited Partnership
Partnership Declaration and registration number
Executed Partnership Agreement
CRA Business Number application data
General Partner identity documents and Canadian contact address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where CRA generates an identity-validation block or pending status notice, call the CRA Business Window and submit scanned verification documents (notarial copy of the Certificate and general partner identification); no additional fee is charged, and the requested effective registration date is preserved if the cure is completed within the CRA compliance window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain CICC Professional Approval and Municipal/Occupational Safety Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) — Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC-IRCC) regulatory division; City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Business Licensing; local fire marshal and OHS authorities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the partnership-level CICC registration application as an immigration and international-student advisory firm, designating a licensed RCIC-IRCC as responsible immigration practitioner; submit the client trust account undertaking executed by a Canadian Schedule I bank or trust company, a governance and conflict-of-interest manual, and the designated RCIC-IRCC endorsement. Concurrently obtain the municipal business licence (services category), the fire safety and occupancy clearance for the office premises, and the WCB/OHS registration before commencing client-facing operations.
required_dossiers: CICC Entity Registration Application and consent of designated RCIC-IRCC
RCIC-IRCC licence endorsement and annual certificate of good standing
Trust account undertaking by a Canadian regulated financial institution
City of Calgary or Edmonton Business Licence Application
Fire safety certificate and occupancy load approval
OHS policy, hazard assessment, and WCB assessment account registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CICC issues a 'Further Information Required' notice, respond with supplementary declarations and updated documents within 30 days to avoid suspension of the application; if the municipal licence is refused or made conditional, apply for reconsideration before the municipal licensing appeal committee; fire-safety deficiencies must be remedied and reinspected at the applicant's cost before the certificate is reissued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) for the regulated immigration-consulting profession; Alberta municipal business licensing authority (City of Calgary / City of Edmonton) for the commercial office advisory operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Regulated International Student Immigration Consulting Firm Licence (RCIC-IRCC / RISIA) and Alberta Municipal Business Licence — Services (Education and Immigration Advisory; ISIC 7810 / NAICS 541199).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) — Environmental Assessment and Approvals Branch.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration-Exempt / Low-Risk Class — the proposed scope comprises a pure office and advisory suite with no industrial manufacturing, no reference-list activity, and no prescribed activity under the Activities Designation Regulation (A.R. 276/2003) Schedule; therefore no full EIA Report or Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act approval is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or industrial VOC emissions; domestic sewage and sanitary effluent must comply with the Alberta municipal sewer use by-law and the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act discharge prohibitions; solid office waste must be handled by licensed municipal waste haulers; HVAC refrigerants must respect the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999, ozone-depleting substance and VOC limits; any interior renovation must comply with the Alberta Asbestos Regulation and workplace indoor-air contaminant limits under the OHS Code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire marshal under the Alberta Fire Code, confirming means of egress, fire alarms, and suppression systems; structural live-load and occupancy clearance under the Alberta Building Code for the office floor; Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) clearance under the OHS Act and OHS Code covering general duty, hazard assessment, first aid, and emergency preparedness; Workers' Compensation Board (WCB) assessment account registration; personal information and client-file security controls in accordance with PIPEDA for immigration advisory records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal tax registration administered via Business Registration Online (BRO) and the 'My Business Account' portal; GST/HST program accounts (RT) issued under the Excise Tax Act (ETA). Provincial contact: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) for LP formation under the Partnership Act (Alberta) and Alberta Treasury Board & Finance for provincial tax matters (Alberta levies no provincial sales tax and no provincial VAT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Alberta Limited Partnership with the Alberta Corporate Registry and obtain the Alberta registration number. Step 2: Apply for the federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online or Form RC1; a non-resident applicant without a Canadian presence must complete Form RC1 with designated foreign contact details and may be required to provide evidence of the place of effective management. Step 3: Open the GST/HST program account (BN-RT0001) with CRA; registration is mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in the trailing four consecutive calendar quarters, but voluntary registration is strongly recommended for a study-abroad/immigration placement LP that intends to zero-rate export advisory services. Step 4: No separate tax identification number is assigned to the LP for income tax purposes; the LP is fiscally transparent and each partner (general and limited) reports its allocable share under ITA s. 96; CRA requires partnership identification of all partners (name, Canadian SIN/BN or foreign tax ID, share percentages) and completion of the T5013 Partnership Information Return with T5013 slips. Step 5: Non-resident partners with Canadian-source business income must either file a Part I corporate/individual return or be subject to Part XIII withholding on passive distributions; a non-resident general partner may need to appoint a Canadian agent or address for service before obtaining clearance certificates (ITA s. 116 applies where the partnership disposes of taxable Canadian property).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The Alberta LP is fiscally transparent for income tax (ITA s. 96): income and losses are computed at the partnership level and allocated to partners in accordance with the limited partnership agreement, with no entity-level federal or Alberta corporate income tax. Territorial_Scope: Canadian-resident partners are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners are taxed only on Canadian-source income (business income carried on through the LP, or passive Canadian-source distributions) subject to applicable tax treaty relief. For GST/HST purposes, the ETA definition of 'person' includes a partnership, so the LP is a distinct registrant holding its own RT account; however, the partners remain jointly and severally liable for the LP's GST/HST remittances. The LP is not a 'tax-exempt zone' entity and has no entitlement to preferential exemption; Alberta's 0% provincial component means only the federal 5% GST applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style 'check-the-box' classification regime; entity classification follows the Partnership Act (Alberta), ITA s. 96, and CRA administrative policy. Available statutory elections relevant to this LP: (i) a non-resident partner may elect under ITA s. 216 to file a Part I return on net Canadian rental/business income instead of facing Part XIII gross-basis withholding; (ii) the LP may elect a non-calendar fiscal period only with CRA authorization — in practice the fiscal period is the calendar year; (iii) under the ETA, the LP may file the s. 156 joint election (closely related entities) for inter-entity supplies and may elect under s. 211 for financial services (generally irrelevant here); (iv) hybrid mismatch arrangements are addressed by ITA ss. 18.4–18.7, which deny a partnership deduction where the same payment is not included in the counterparty jurisdiction (or is deductible elsewhere); such arrangements must be disclosed under the mandatory disclosure rules (ITA s. 237.3) on Form RC312 or RC313. No provincial election exists for LP pass-through classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) — Canada's federal value-added tax. Alberta has no provincial sales tax and no HST provincial component; only the 5% federal GST applies. Study-abroad placement, university-admission processing, and immigration-visa advisory services are taxable supplies unless an express exemption applies (e.g., legal services rendered by a licensed lawyer or educational services supplied by a school authority; regulated immigration consultants are not exempt merely because they are licensed).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (general 'small supplier' threshold: total worldwide gross revenue from taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies, in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; a person exceeding CAD 30,000 in any single quarter or in the trailing four-quarter period must register for GST/HST. Non-resident suppliers carrying on business in Canada are subject to the same threshold. Below the threshold registration is voluntary; the LP should voluntarily register to recover input tax credits and to legally claim zero-rating on export supplies of advisory services).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, CTC authorization, digital stamping, or pre-clearance e-invoice regime comparable to Mexico/Italy. CRA has adopted a voluntary Pan-Canadian Trust Framework and PEPPOL-based e-invoicing standard (Canadian Digital Interoperability Blueprint); adoption is accelerating for B2G transactions but remains non-mandatory. Mandatory statutory requirements under the ETA: (i) all GST/HST registrants with annual gross revenue exceeding CAD 1.5 million must file returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or approved EDI; (ii) every tax invoice must state the supplier's BN/RT registration number, invoice date, recipient name, description of supplies, consideration, GST payable (or explicit 'zero-rated — Schedule VI' notation), and, where applicable, the recipient's BN; (iii) simplified invoices (minimum content) are permitted for supplies under CAD 30; (iv) electronic records and invoices must be retained for six years (or longer where CRA requires) in a readable format, and e-invoices must be produced in a format that CRA can access.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 of the Excise Tax Act, a supply of advisory, consulting, placement, or immigration-processing services is zero-rated where all of the following are satisfied: (i) the recipient is a non-resident of Canada at the time the supply is made — verified by foreign passport, permanent-establishment location, or foreign tax-residency certificate; (ii) the recipient is not a GST/HST registrant in respect of the supply; (iii) the service does not relate to real property situated in Canada nor to tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed; and (iv) the service is not otherwise deemed to be supplied in, or consumed in, Canada. Offshore study-abroad placement consulting, international student recruitment, Canadian university-application assistance, and golden-visa residence advisory services supplied to a non-resident client from the Alberta LP generally qualify for zero-rating. In contrast, services performed for a foreign national physically present in Canada at the time of performance (e.g., in-Canada study-permit extension, post-arrival settlement, or immigration file prosecution with Canadian government filings) are ordinarily performed in Canada and consumed in Canada — those services are taxable at 5% GST and may NOT be zero-rated. The LP must document the non-resident status of the recipient at the exact time of billing and maintain a per-client export analysis.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed retainer/engagement contract identifying the non-resident recipient, the scope of study-abroad/immigration services, the place of performance, and the contractual situs of the supply
Tax invoice displaying the LP's BN/RT registration number, invoice date, consideration, and the explicit notation 'GST/HST zero-rated pursuant to Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7, ETA' with CAD 0.00 GST

Incoming wire transfer / SWIFT MT103 / foreign-currency remittance advice evidencing receipt of non-resident consideration within the 180-day repatriation window, together with FX conversion records and the LP's foreign-currency bank statement

Non-resident status substantiation pack: foreign passport bio-page or foreign national ID, foreign address confirmation, and foreign tax-residency certificate (where the client is an entity: certificate of incorporation, registered office outside Canada, and confirmation that the client has no Canadian permanent establishment)

Canadian customs B13A Export Declaration is required ONLY where incidental physical goods (e.g., branded brochures, printed application kits, or marketing collateral) are exported cross-border; for pure service exports no customs declaration is filed, but an internal export register must document each contract, recipient, invoice, and wire receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits of export zero-rating focus on four elements: (1) genuineness of the non-resident status of the recipient; (2) absence of Canadian consumption or Canadian situs of the service; (3) sufficiency of contemporaneous documentation; and (4) timely FX repatriation of fees within 180 days. Where CRA determines that a supply was incorrectly zero-rated, it will reassess GST at 5% on the full consideration, charge compound daily interest at the prescribed rate (currently tiered, approximately 8%-10% annually), and may impose: (i) a late-filing/omission penalty under ETA s. 280 of 5% of the net tax amount plus 1% per full month of delay (maximum 12 months); (ii) a gross-negligence penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and 5% of the understated tax where the false zero-rating claim was made knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence; (iii) revocation or clawback of any input tax credits and rebates previously claimed, with repayment of refunds plus interest; and (iv) criminal prosecution for tax evasion under ETA s. 327 — on summary conviction, fines of up to 50% of the evaded tax and/or imprisonment up to 2 years; on indictment, fines of up to 200% of the evaded tax and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. The ordinary reassessment window is four years from the original filing; the window is indefinite in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or willful default. Because the LP is a partnership, all general partners (and limited partners to the extent of their involvement in the management or their distributions) are jointly and severally liable for the GST/HST assessment, interest, and penalties; CRA may also assess culpable officers or partners for failure to exercise due diligence in the collection and remittance of GST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the central banking and monetary authority, with exchange-control policy residing in the Crown through the Minister of Finance under the Currency Act and the Exchange Fund Act. There is no dedicated foreign-exchange administration; OSFI supervises authorised deposit-taking institutions, and FINTRAC enforces AML/CFT obligations under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada provides de jure full convertibility for both current-account and capital-account transactions. The Canadian dollar freely floats in the interbank market, and no licence, approval, or repatriation permit is required for inward capital contributions, fee disbursements, loan repayments, or profit distributions. Remittance hurdles are exclusively tax-regulatory: (i) the Alberta LP's business income allocated to non-resident limited partners is generally taxable in Canada under Part I of the Income Tax Act; (ii) guaranteed payments, management fees, interest, and royalties paid or credited to non-residents attract 25% Part XIII withholding (treaty-reduced in most jurisdictions); (iii) GST/HST zero-rating of exported consulting services to non-residents is preserved only with complete documentary evidence of the client's non-residency and the place-of-consumption analysis. No exchange-control-based barrier exists to converting or remitting CAD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no minimum conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export receipts. The LP may retain foreign-currency earnings from international-student placement and immigration-visa advisory services in domestic or offshore foreign-currency accounts indefinitely. For tax purposes, foreign-currency income must be translated into CAD at the Bank of Canada noon spot rate for the relevant date under section 261 of the Income Tax Act, and Form T1135 is required when the cost amount of specified foreign property exceeds CAD 100,000. All electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more (including 24-hour aggregates) are automatically reportable to FINTRAC.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Client Trust / Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account and USD Foreign-Currency Clearing Account
Cross-Border Client Escrow Account with strong Asia/Latin America correspondent network

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary settlement liquidity, Low for fiduciary trust functions. Offshore digital EMIs and fintech platforms (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, etc.) must register as money services businesses with FINTRAC and obtain a licence under Alberta's Money Services Businesses Act to lawfully hold or transmit funds for Canadian clients. They can process high-volume low-value payments to overseas universities and visa authorities, but they lack access to Canada's Lynx domestic clearing system and cannot serve as the principal bank. CICC rules require all immigration-consulting client funds to be held in a segregated trust account at a Canadian-regulated deposit-taking institution, which EMIs cannot provide.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the general partner's authorized directors and for any limited partner owning 25% or more of the partnership. FINTRAC's prescribed identification methods allow remote opening only through a credit-file-based or reliable-external-source process; in practice, Schedule I banks require an in-person or notarized-juristic-person verification and, for Medium-Risk-Enhanced immigration consultancies, a mandatory documented compliance interview. A Canadian lawyer referral can streamline acceptance, but it does not waive beneficial-ownership identification. The bank will require the original Alberta Corporate Registry certificate, the notarized partnership agreement, the Register of Partners, and, where the general partner is non-resident, evidence of an appointed Alberta agent for service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity of a non-resident limited partnership with multiple foreign partners or nominee/trust arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized LP agreement; certified Alberta Corporate Registry extract; updated Register of Limited Partners; general-partner certificate quantifying each partner's ownership percentage; corporate organigram; passport copies of all individuals and registry extracts for all corporate partners; written UBO attestation executed by each 25%+ partner; and a sanctions-list/adverse-media screening report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border wire volume originating from FATF-watchlisted or high-risk jurisdictions (tuition and visa payments from certain source markets).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying student admission contracts; visa-application reference numbers; CAQ or study-permit correspondence; itemised invoices from universities and immigration authorities; source-of-funds bank statements for each wire; full sanctions screening results; and a documented commercial rationale memorandum maintained per remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEPs) or their family members using the golden-visa/immigration pathway as the transaction's sole driver.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-declaration form; source-of-wealth report covering assets and professional history; independent verification of funds from a regulated financial institution; senior-compliance sign-off memo; and the executed service engagement confirming that funds represent consultancy fees, not investment or settlement monies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual trust-account activity: clustering of large inbound deposits followed by rapid outbound disbursements to overseas universities, banks, or visa offices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated trust-account ledger; approved disbursement schedule; due-diligence file for each payee; professional undertaking by the licensed Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant; CICC trust-account compliance confirmation; monthly reconciliation statements with the bank; and proof of professional-liability insurance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory-licence gap or immigration-consulting regulation exposure while the LP holds client money.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CICC registration certificate for the responsible RCIC; a certified copy of any governing licence or exemption; provincial consumer-protection registration where applicable; errors-and-omissions insurance binder; and the firm's regulatory complaint history or good-standing letter.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (i) execute a capital-call notice and subscription agreement before transfer; (ii) route each wire via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign partner's own same-name bank account to the LP's account at a Schedule I bank; (iii) insert 'LP capital contribution — capital call no. [X]' in SWIFT field 70; (iv) identify the transaction narrative as 'capital contribution to Canadian limited partnership' for Statistics Canada balance-of-payments and FINTRAC coding; (v) provide source-of-funds documentation and a completed partner KYC file at onboarding; (vi) recognise that every wire of CAD 10,000 or more (or 24-hour aggregate) triggers FINTRAC EFT/large-transaction reporting; (vii) file an Investment Canada Act notification for non-WTO partners where applicable. No Minister of Finance or exchange-control approval is required for establishing a new Canadian business by a WTO investor.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rails: (1) CAD settlements to domestic universities, colleges, and authorities use the Lynx high-value real-time gross settlement system via the bank's treasury desk, with EFT for smaller payments; (2) USD/EUR/GBP/CNH outbound payments settle through SWIFT MT103 over the correspondent network, using Fedwire/CHIPS for USD, TARGET2 for EUR, and CIPS/CHATS for CNH, with field 50K identifying the LP, field 57A the beneficiary bank, and field 70 the student or application reference; (3) commercial letters of credit (UCP600) are permissible but atypical for services, and standby LCs are suitable only for large institutional placement contracts; (4) trust-account disbursements must be approved by the licensed RCIC and settled exclusively from the segregated trust ledger, never from the operational account; and (5) every outbound EFT of CAD 10,000 or more requires beneficiary KYC and an underlying purpose statement for FINTRAC reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP, and CAD/CNH forward contracts with a Schedule I Canadian bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's standard dealing terms
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing INR, VND, PHP, THB, TRY, and other restricted-deliverability currencies to hedge receipt-side foreign-client fee exposures
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) for medium-term alignment of non-resident partner capital contributions with expected profit distributions
Vanilla over-the-counter FX options (purchased calls and puts) to cap adverse conversion movements without limiting upside
FX spot contracts for near-dated operational settlement, with no leveraged retail FX trading permitted for the LP
Rolling one-month forward micro-hedges for university tuition disbursements, consistent with the LP's pass-through tax profile and T1135 reporting obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Limited Partnership — Annual Return (annual registration confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service Alberta Corporate Registry (Registrar of Partnerships, Government of Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary date of the LP's original registration; continuous annual cycle (Alberta Partnership Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. P-3, s. 68)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing attracts registrar notice; continued default (typically two consecutive missed cycles) allows administrative cancellation/strike-off of LP registration; cancellation removes the statutory limited-liability shield of limited partners for post-cancellation obligations; reinstatement requires service of arrears and registrar order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013), T5013 Summary and partner allocation slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end (May 31 for a December 31 year-end); partner slips distributed by the same deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return: $100 Cdn per month per partner (minimum $100); late/incorrect slips: $100 Cdn per slip per day (max $7,500, or $25,000 for repeat/uncertified filings); prescribed-rate interest; prosecution under Income Tax Act ss. 238/239 for grave non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST return (Form GST34 for periodic filers; annual return for annual-filer registrants) with payment of 5% federal GST collected on consulting and management fees (Alberta has no provincial sales tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: One month after the end of each reporting period; annual-filer returns and balance due within three months after fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar year-end); registration mandatory once taxable revenues exceed $30,000 Cdn in a single quarter or cumulatively
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: 5% of unpaid net tax plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months); per-day penalties for nil-return defaults; interest compounded daily at prescribed CRA rates; dishonest or wilful evasion subject to criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) licences for each licensed consultant providing immigration and study-permit advisory services through the LP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC), Canada's statutory regulator under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the CICC licence anniversary date; continuing-education and practice-certificate requirements must be satisfied before renewal (typically by the CICC annual renewal cycle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Practice without a current RCIC licence is an offence under s. 91 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (summary or indictable, up to 2 years' imprisonment on indictment); CICC may suspend, revoke, or discipline the consultant; the LP's business continuity is impaired while consultants are unlicensed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The Alberta Partnership Act and the federal Income Tax Act impose no statutory audit on limited partnerships. A full independent audit becomes mandatory only where the partnership agreement or an external covenant so requires, where a corporate limited partner's own statutory audit regime necessitates audited partnership accounts (equity-method reporting), where CICC imposes an external financial review in a disciplinary or practice-review process, or where a lender mandates financial-statement assurance. Absent such triggers, a notice-to-reader or review-engagement package is the market standard.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private Canadian partnerships normally report under Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook); IFRS applies only if the LP becomes a publicly accountable enterprise or an investor/regulator requires IFRS. The general partner must keep records sufficient to support T5013 income/loss allocations and GST/HST reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO filing exists for Alberta LPs at the current registry level. The general partner must nevertheless perform an annual confirmation at each registration anniversary: update the Register of Limited Partners for transfers, contributions, and new limited partners; re-run identity verification and AML/CDD screening for every partner and any individual with a 25%-or-greater economic or voting interest; file a Notice of Change with Service Alberta within 30 days where registered information (general partner, registered office, or place of business) has changed; and minute the confirmation. Federal beneficial-ownership registry legislation for non-corporate vehicles is under development and may impose a future shareholder-style UBO filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (capital contributions, dates, transfers and redemption records — required by the Alberta Partnership Act)
Register of General Partners (identity, addresses and administrative history — required by the Alberta Partnership Act)
Minute Book (general partner resolutions, partner consents and annual confirmation records)
Registered Office and Registered Agent record with copies of Service Alberta registrations and annual returns

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Alberta general corporate rate of 23% (15% federal + 8% Alberta) applied at the corporate-partner level; the Alberta Limited Partnership itself is fiscally transparent with no entity-level corporate income tax, and income flows through to partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (9% federal + 2% Alberta on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income for eligible Canadian-controlled corporate partners); SR&ED refundable investment tax credits; intercorporate dividend deduction; 20-year non-capital loss carryforward; no Alberta capital tax or provincial payroll tax for partnerships without employees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Summary – Partnership Information Return (CRA My Business Account portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within five months after the end of the partnership fiscal period; the LP may elect a non-calendar fiscal period subject to the s.249.1(4) deferral rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership legal name, Alberta LP registration number, business address, fiscal period, and responsible partner name.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure a Canadian business address is reported; non-resident partners are identified in Part 2 for Canadian-source income allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from study-abroad placement and immigration visa advisory fees, deductible expenses, and net business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate Canadian-source advisory fees from foreign-source fees; Part XIII or Part XII.2 withholding may apply on distributions of Canadian-source income to non-resident partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share of income, loss, and tax credits allocated to each partner per the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must report their allocated share of Canadian-source income on a T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; ordinary partnership distributions are not subject to dividend withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business activity code (NAICS 541199 / ISIC 7810) and related-party transaction disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form T106 if the aggregate value of non-arm's length cross-border transactions exceeds CAD 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500 under s.162(1.1); additional penalties for failure to provide complete information; prescribed-rate interest compounds daily on any unpaid balance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: GST/HST Return (Form GST34) filed via CRA My Business Account
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (mandatory registration once annual taxable revenue exceeds CAD 30,000)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due one month after the end of the reporting period; annual filers remit within three months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total GST/HST collected on taxable advisory fees charged to clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Supplies of advisory services to non-resident students may be zero-rated under the place-of-supply rules if the services are not performed in connection with Canadian real property or tangible personal property; legal determination required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Input tax credits claimed on Canadian operating expenses such as rent, marketing, and staff salaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot personally claim ITCs for partnership expenses incurred outside the partnership's GST registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax remitted after ITCs and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A deemed election under ETA s.226(4) may apply if a non-resident partner fails to file an annual return; confirm before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Bad debt adjustment for uncollected student placement fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign receivables written off in Canada require supporting collection evidence; maintain escrow account documentation for student clients.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Penalty of 1% of the net tax remitted late, plus a 25% penalty on the unpaid amount for a second failure within two years; statutory interest at the prescribed rate plus 3% compounded daily.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Alberta AT1 Corporate Income Tax Return (filed by each corporate partner claiming the LP allocation)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within six months after the corporate partner's taxation year-end; balance of tax due within two months (or three months for eligible CCPCs) under s.157.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate partner legal name, jurisdiction of incorporation, and CRA business number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign corporate partners must open a CRA account and file T2 solely to report Canadian-source income allocated from the LP.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Flow-through income or loss from the Alberta LP included in taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty relief for existing permanent establishment or claim an exemption where the LP activity does not create a PE for the foreign corporate partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta prorating of taxable income and application of the 8% Alberta corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners with a permanent establishment in Alberta must file AT1 and pay Alberta corporate tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer-pricing information return and Country-by-Country notification where thresholds are exceeded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach T106 before the T2 filing deadline; late filing exposes the partner to transfer-pricing documentation penalties under s.247(3).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; no-filing penalties for nil balance; instalment interest on corporate partners; Alberta late-payment interest at prescribed rates.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% gross Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder, reduced by treaty to typically 15% for portfolio holdings and 5% for substantial shareholdings (e.g., 10% or greater voting control under the Canada-US treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident partner obtains a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, submits it with CRA Form NR301 to the payor/withholding agent, and may apply under Form NR6 to remit Part XIII withholding quarterly on non-resident partnership allocations; CRA grants treaty-based relief only if the partnership has sufficient Canadian economic substance and the partner certifies treaty entitlement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory Part XIII rate, generally reduced to 10% under most Canadian DTAs including the Canada-US treaty; interest: 25% statutory, wholly or partially exempt under most treaties for arm's-length interest (Canada-US treaty generally exempts arm's-length interest); partnership allocations of active business income are not treated as dividends but remain Canadian-source income reportable by the non-resident partner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate value of non-arm's length cross-border transactions per taxation year triggers mandatory T106 filing and contemporaneous Local File documentation; Country-by-Country notification (RC4646) applies when the consolidated group revenue exceeds CAD 750,000,000; Master File and Local File must exist prior to the filing deadline to avoid s.247(3) penalties.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No formal Economic Substance Regulations statute in Canada; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s.245) and s.247 transfer-pricing rules require documented risk-reward capacity including employees physically performing study-abroad placement and visa-admission decision-making in Alberta; a shell LP with no operational substance will be denied loss allocations, treaty relief, and GST registrations, and will be recharacterized as a sham partnership subject to deemed dividend treatment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report T5013 allocations, inflating or fabricating immigration-visa deductible expenses, diverting advisory fees to undisclosed foreign bank accounts, or knowingly filing false returns under s.239(1).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of 50%–200% of the evaded tax plus imprisonment up to 2 years on summary conviction or up to 5 years on indictment; civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the understated tax; s.163(2) penalties of CAD 50,000 for false statements or omission of income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners jointly and severally liable for corporate unpaid tax, penalties, and interest; conviction can trigger travel bans and passport seizure; restitution orders apply to personal assets of directors found to have directed the evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Immigration Practice and AML Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in immigration and visa representation without proper licensing by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC/RCIC), or accepting student-trust funds without required escrow and anti-money laundering client due diligence under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: IRPA s.91 penalties up to CAD 100,000 per unlicensed immigration consultant and/or imprisonment up to 2 years on indictment; AML administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation plus criminal sanctions for money laundering under s.462.31; suspension of business licences by Alberta Consumer Protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unlicensed immigration activity fines when they direct or supervise the offence; senior officers face prohibition orders; FINTRAC penalty regime assigns direct liability to directors for failure to implement an AML compliance program.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Alberta LP with no office, no operational staff, no CICC-licensed consultant, and allocation of more than 90% of study-abroad income to a zero-tax offshore corporate partner without substantive activities, constituting a sham partnership and treaty-shopping arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR denial of the tax benefit under s.245(2); transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the net adjustment under s.247(3); recharacterization of profit allocations as deemed Part XIII dividends subject to 25% withholding and arrears interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Limited partners forfeit limited-liability protection if they take part in management under Alberta Limited Partnership Act s.13; general partner and directors are personally assessed for the disallowed tax and penalties where the corporate partner is insolvent or the allocation is a mere conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file Form T1135 for foreign income and property held through a foreign trust, nominee account in a zero-tax jurisdiction, or failure to file CbC notification (RC4646) and T106 for related-party cross-border transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: T1135 penalty of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500; after formal demand, a penalty of 5% per month of the unreported property's cost amount up to 24 months; failure to file T106 exposes 10% transfer-pricing penalty and Canadian criminal prosecution for false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and partners civilly liable for unreported foreign property penalties; criminal indictment allows court-ordered asset freezes and travel bans; CRS/FATCA automatic exchange disclosures expose the structure to global tax administration review.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Collecting GST/HST on advisory fees without remitting, using input tax credits on unregistered foreign suppliers, or failing to remit source deductions for Canadian employees through the CRA payroll account (PD7A).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GST penalty of 1% plus 25% of the unpaid net tax on repeat failures; payroll penalties of 10%–20% of unremitted source deductions plus interest; director's liability under s.323 ETA and s.227.1 ITA for unremitted GST and employee withholdings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for all unremitted GST/HST and payroll source deductions without a defence, enabling CRA to pursue personal bank accounts, impose liens, and obtain court enforcement orders including temporary travel restrictions.
